channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: SPOTLIGHT
item.description: Adam Barron is an independent Middle East political analyst and consultant, specialising primarily in Yemen, where he has reported from the capital, Sanaa, for The Economist. He writes for Foreign Policy and The Atlantic.
item.dc:creator: Gavin LEE

item.title: At least two killed, multiple people wounded in attack on Riyadh airport
item.description: At least two people were killed in an attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Saturday, including an Egyptian flight attendant, according to a medical source at a local hospital. Earlier this week, another attack on the airport by the Houthis killed three people and damaged a plane, though the Iran-backed group did not announce any new attacks on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Convicted murderer Christa Pike leaves hospital, returns to prison after botched execution
item.description: Christa Pike's lawyers on Saturday said that the 50-year-old convicted murderer has been discharged from the hospital and returned to prison. Pike was transported to the hospital in critical condition on September 30 after she survived Tennessee's botched effort to execute her for murdering a classmate when she was a teenager.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: 🔴 Live: Trump lashes out at Zelensky, says Ukraine needs new president who will agree to end war
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: India protests: New 'cockroach' movement leader named
item.description:
Indian police detained the head of the satirical "cockroach" online movement on Saturday, the group said, ahead of a major protest against the Election Commission that prompted strict security measures.
"They seem to have seen that coming," notes France 24's Andrew Hilliar. In a prerecorded video, Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Party, names an interim leader to take over.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: South Africa: Anti-migrant unrest flares in Durban
item.description: Police in Durban were battling a fresh wave of anti-migrant unrest. Shops were looted, homes were torched and foreign nationals were targeted as crowds took to the streets for a second day. The violence has revived fears of rising xenophobic tensions over immigration.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Kenya: Ebola tests negative as contact tracing continues
item.description: Tests have come back negative for a person suspected of having Ebola who was reportedly in quarantine at a hospital, following rumours circulating over the past 24 hours. Meanwhile, in Nairobi, authorities are racing to trace contacts of Kenya's first Ebola death, reported on Monday. Our correspondent Bastien Renouil tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
item.description: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections due next month until September 11, ​2027, and called ‌a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the ⁠delay. Our correspondent in Jerusalem Noga Tarnopolsky tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Midterms: "It does look like the Republicans will lose control of the House of Representatives"
item.description: Most of the political world is focused on next month's midterm elections in the US. "It does look like the Republicans will lose control of the House of Representatives," says our guest, Bruce Stokes, a visiting senior fellow at the German Marshall Fund of the United States.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: French cycling prodigy Seixas claims first Monument victory at Giro di Lombardia
item.description: French prodigy Paul Seixas claimed his first Monument win at the Giro di Lombardia on Saturday. The victory makes the 20-year-old the fourth-youngest winner of a Monument race.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: War in Ukraine: Russian strikes kill 15, including a young girl
item.description:
Early Saturday, Russia targeted residential neighbourhoods in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia with "five guided aerial bombs", according to Ukraine's National Police.
At least 15 people were killed, including three children, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said. The family of a young girl killed in the attack was inconsolable.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: India detains thousands, locks down Delhi to foil election chief protest
item.description: Police detained more than 2,000 protesters and the founder of the "cockroach" youth movement in Delhi on Saturday as security forces locked down parts of the capital to thwart a rally demanding the resignation of India's election chief. Our correspondent Navodita Kumari tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Death penalty: Why are executions increasing worldwide?
item.description: October 10 marks the World Day Against the Death Penalty. This week, the EU condemned capital punishment as a cruel and degrading form of punishment. But not all world leaders share this view. We discuss why executions are on the rise with our guest François Picard, host of "Death Row Stories".
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Russian attack on Ukrainian city kills 15, a day after Trump eases diesel sanctions on Moscow
item.description: Fifteen people, including three children, were killed in a Russian attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia on Saturday, a day after US President Donald Trump announced a deal to lift sanctions on Russian diesel, in a major setback for Kyiv. Our correspondent Gulliver Cragg tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: India detains 'cockroach' movement leaders in bid to thwart election protest
item.description: Indian police detained the head of the satirical "cockroach" online movement on Saturday as hundreds of protesters demanding the election commissioner's resignation gathered in New Delhi despite a heavy security crackdown.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Lens see off Lyon as Ligue 1 season resumes after international break
item.description: Lens put an end to a four-match winless run by beating Lyon 2-1 on Friday night, in what was the first Ligue 1 fixture after a three-week international break. Paris Saint-Germain head coach Luis Enrique has brushed off concerns about Ousmane Dembélé's recent form, having rested the forward for Saturday's match against promoted side Le Mans.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Portugal hits Ronaldo with provisional suspension for walking out on national team
item.description: Portuguese Football Federation announced on Saturday that it has provisionally suspended star attacker Cristiano Ronaldo and opened disciplinary proceedings against the 41-year-old over his decision to walk out on the national team last month.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Yemen says advancing against Houthis around key Bab al-Mandab strait
item.description: Yemen said Saturday that forces were advancing against the Houthis around the Bab al-Mandab strait, a week after the country's Saudi-backed government announced that it was initiating a counter-offensive to take back territory seized by the pro-Iran group during last month's lightning offensive. In Riyadh, diplomatic sources reported a missile attack on the civilian airport, with at least five Saudi nationals wounded being treated in intensive care.
item.source: © Southern Giants Brigades Media Office via AP
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Trump, Zelensky clash over diesel deal as Russian strikes on Ukraine kill 21, including children
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Saturday told reporters that Ukraine should "get a new president", adding that his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky had disobeyed his orders not to strike Russian refineries. This comes after Washington moved to ease sanctions on Russian diesel and as Moscow's strikes on Ukraine, including the city of Zaporizhzhia, killed at least 21 people.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: 🔴 Palestinian president Abbas postpones legislative elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Palestinian president Abbas postpones legislative, presidential elections to September 2027
item.description: ⁠⁠Palestinian president ​Mahmoud ​Abbas announced on Saturday that legislative ⁠elections would be postponed from November ​28 to September ​11, 2027, the ​official Palestinian news agency ⁠WAFA reported. In his presidential decree, Abbas set the next presidential elections for that day as well.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: October 7 scars push Israel's first-time voters to right
item.description: Like hundreds of thousands of Israelis, Amihai will be of voting age for the first time since Hamas carried out its attack on October 7, 2023. When he casts his ballot this month, he has one priority above all -- security.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Hunger and malnutrition stalk Gazans, a year on from ceasefire
item.description: Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a community kitchen in the hope of getting some food for her family. It has been a year since a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel was supposed to allow food to flood into the ruined territory, yet widespread hunger persists there.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Severe injuries at French student protests draw scrutiny to police tactics
item.description: Twenty-four investigations have been opened by French police watchdog IGPN into incidents linked to the ongoing high school protest movement, the interior ministry said. The police response has reignited calls to scrap rubber bullets and launcher-fired riot-control weapons, long denounced by rights groups and UN experts as dangerous and excessive.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24
